**Finding: Compliant (no redline).**

The agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right running against Mortgage Logic.com as Client, and no vendor right of access to our systems for usage verification. Targeted searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor" and "books" returned no hits, and the two sections the playbook flags as likely homes for such a right contain only customer-favourable provisions:

- **§ 5–6 (Compensation / Documentation and Disputes)** — the information right runs in *our* favour: TrueLink must supply documentation supporting charges on request, and we may contest charges (subject to timely payment of contested amounts).
- **§ 8 (Client covenants)** — compliance, access-restriction and content warranties only; no examination or verification right. § 2.e in fact gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files.

Since no audit right binds us at all, our position is stronger than the playbook's preferred limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so there is nothing to constrain and flagging would only invite the counterparty to add a right that does not currently exist.

One item noted for awareness rather than as a deviation: § 8.f permits TrueLink "at any time to implement technical mechanisms" to prevent spamming. That is an enforcement measure applied to TrueLink's own Interface, not an audit of our records or systems, so it belongs to the acceptable-use analysis rather than this rule.
